about: Trimmed subset of EU clause references used by the c4-guardrails rules. Ids follow REGIME:DOC:REF. Titles are the official article titles; summaries are our own short paraphrases, not legal text and not legal advice. Only the texts published in the Official Journal of the European Union are authentic.

clauses.title: Record-keeping
clauses.summary: High-risk AI systems have to be able to record events automatically (logs) across their lifetime so that their operation can be traced and monitored.

clauses.title: Human oversight
clauses.summary: High-risk AI systems have to be designed so that people can oversee them effectively while in use, proportionate to risk, autonomy and context. For other AI systems this is a widely used design practice.

clauses.title: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems (retention of logs)
clauses.summary: Deployers keep the logs a high-risk AI system generates under their control for an appropriate period, at least six months unless other law says otherwise.

clauses.instrument: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1774 (DORA RTS on ICT risk management)
clauses.title: Logging
clauses.summary: Financial entities define and run logging procedures and tools: which events are logged, how long logs are kept and how log data is protected.

clauses.title: General principles for the management of ICT third-party risk
clauses.summary: Financial entities stay responsible when they rely on ICT third-party providers and manage that risk inside their ICT risk management framework, including concentration risk.

clauses.title: General principles for the management of ICT third-party risk (exit strategies)
clauses.summary: For ICT services that support critical or important functions, financial entities need exit strategies that let them leave a provider without disrupting the business.

clauses.title: Data protection by design and by default
clauses.summary: Controllers build appropriate technical and organisational measures into the design of processing and, by default, process only the personal data each purpose needs.

clauses.title: Security of processing
clauses.summary: Controllers and processors apply security measures appropriate to the risk, such as encryption, resilience, recovery and regular testing.

clauses.title: Security of processing (pseudonymisation and encryption)
clauses.summary: Pseudonymisation and encryption of personal data are named as examples of appropriate security measures.

clauses.title: General principle for transfers
clauses.summary: Personal data leaves the EU/EEA only under the conditions of GDPR Chapter V, so knowing where a recipient processes data matters.

clauses.title: Transfers subject to appropriate safeguards
clauses.summary: Without an adequacy decision, a transfer to a third country needs appropriate safeguards such as standard data protection clauses.

clauses.title: Cybersecurity risk-management measures (supply chain security)
clauses.summary: Risk-management measures cover supply chain security, including the relationship with direct suppliers and service providers.

clauses.title: Cybersecurity risk-management measures (cryptography and encryption)
clauses.summary: Risk-management measures include policies on the use of cryptography and, where appropriate, encryption.

clauses.title: Cybersecurity risk-management measures (access control and asset management)
clauses.summary: Risk-management measures include access control policies and asset management, which covers how credentials are held.

clauses.title: Cybersecurity risk-management measures (authentication and secured communications)
clauses.summary: Risk-management measures include multi-factor or continuous authentication and secured communications where appropriate.

clauses.title: Monitoring and logging
clauses.summary: In-scope entities monitor and log activity on their network and information systems, decide what is logged, review logs and keep them for a defined period.

clauses.title: Network segmentation
clauses.summary: In-scope entities segment systems into zones by risk, keep critical systems in secured zones and restrict traffic between zones to what operation needs.
